chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkinn (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Abu Ja'far al-Asamm, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the spirit that was in Adam (peace be upon him) and the one that was in 'Isa (peace be upon him), what are they? He (peace be upon him) replied: 'They are two created spirits, which He chose and selected, the spirit of Adam (peace be upon him) and the spirit of 'Isa (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: What is the nature of the spirit breathed into Adam and Jesus according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ontological status of the *ruh* breathed into Adam and *Isa, affirming that they are two distinct, created entities rather than a single uncreated divine essence. This distinction supports the Shia theological view that while the spirit is a noble creation chosen by Allah, it remains contingent and not identical to the Divine Essence itself, resolving ambiguities in verses like 'I breathed into him of My Spirit.'

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 4. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (RA) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of `Umar ibn Udhaynah, on the authority of Abu Ja`far al-Asamm that

I asked Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (AS) about the spirits that were in Adam (AS) and `Isa (AS). He (AS) replied, “They were two created spirits. Allah chose and selected them as the spirit of Adam and the spirit of `Isa (as).
